::: info IDS-FROM-THE-RUNTIME
**Leave the id out of an INSERT**

Give each table an INTEGER PRIMARY KEY (or a TEXT key) and leave it out of every INSERT: the runtime chooses it. Read a new row's id back with last\_insert\_rowid() or RETURNING id. Never compute one (max(id) + 1) and never write a number for it. Ids are large and are not in the order rows were added across copies, so order by a column of your own (a position, a date), not by id.

**Why.** Every copy draws ids from its own range, so two people adding a row offline never pick the same one. A number the application writes is the same id on every copy, and two rows written with it become one row, merged and flagged.

<small>Applies to every shape · checked by the lint (`literal-id`); refused at run time · [IDS-FROM-THE-RUNTIME in Constraints](/docs/constraints#IDS-FROM-THE-RUNTIME)</small>
:::
